objectives.title: Architecture standards
objectives.statement: Design agents to the organization's architecture standards and patterns, so that they can be maintained and can work with each other.
objectives.risk: Inconsistent designs that are hard to maintain
objectives.metric: Share of agents that conform to the architecture standards
tiers: Experiments may use any pattern inside the sandbox.
The design uses approved patterns, or records why it does not.
An architect reviews conformance before build starts.
The architecture board approves the design and any exception.
objectives.evidence: The design record, the patterns it uses, and the review decision.

objectives.title: Right-sized agents
objectives.statement: Scope each agent to one job it can do well, so that designs do not grow complicated and drift beyond their purpose.
objectives.risk: Agents that grow beyond their purpose
objectives.metric: Average number of declared offerings per agent
tiers: No limit applies in a sandbox.
The design states the one job the agent does.
An architect challenges any agent that declares more than one job.
Any agent that combines jobs needs a written reason approved by the architecture board.
objectives.evidence: The agent's declared offerings and the design review that accepted them.

objectives.title: Declared scope and refusals
objectives.statement: Write down what each agent does and what it refuses to do, and sign that declaration, so that its scope is clear to anyone who relies on it.
objectives.risk: Agents that drift into other agents' work
objectives.metric: Share of agents with a signed declaration of what they do and refuse
tiers: The owner describes the experiment's scope in a sentence.
The agent has a written declaration of its offerings and refusals.
The declaration is signed and published with every version.
The declaration is checked by someone other than the builder, and conformance to it is tested at release.
objectives.evidence: The signed declaration for the version that is running.

objectives.title: Explainability
objectives.statement: Design agents so that each decision and act can be explained afterwards, from records of what the agent saw and did.
objectives.metric: Share of agents whose decisions can be traced step by step
tiers: The experiment keeps a log of its runs.
Each act is recorded with its inputs and result.
Every step, model call and tool call is traced, so a single run can be followed from start to finish.
Explanations can be produced for an affected person or a regulator on request, within a set time.
objectives.evidence: Trace records for sampled runs, and the time taken to answer explanation requests.

objectives.title: Interoperability
objectives.statement: Design agents to standard interfaces and protocols, so that they can work with existing systems and with other agents.
objectives.risk: Agents that cannot work with other systems
tiers: No requirement applies in a sandbox.
The agent uses the organization's approved protocols for messages and tools.
Integration with each declared dependency is tested before release.
Integration is tested with the partners and systems outside the organization that the agent will deal with.
objectives.evidence: The declared interfaces and the integration test results for the current version.

objectives.title: Security by design
objectives.statement: Review security at design time, so that the harm an agent could do is limited before it is given any credentials.
objectives.metric: Share of agents with a design-time security review
tiers: The experiment has no production credentials.
A standard threat checklist is completed for the design.
A security reviewer sets the limits on what the agent can reach and do before build starts.
The security review includes a threat model reviewed by a second security reviewer.
objectives.evidence: The completed checklist or threat model, and the limits it set.

objectives.title: Design review
objectives.statement: Review and approve the design of every agent at Tier 2 or above before development begins.
objectives.metric: Share of Tier 2 and higher agents with an approved design
tiers: No design review is required.
A peer reviews the design.
The architecture board reviews the design in full.
The architecture board reviews the design, and the executive sponsor approves it.
objectives.evidence: The design review record with the reviewers and their decision.

objectives.title: Finding ungoverned agents
objectives.statement: Look for agents running without governance, and bring them under it through a simple path that does not punish the people who built them.
tiers: Builders are told how to register an experiment.
Network and spending data are scanned each quarter for agent activity that is not in the catalog.
Scans run each month, and an agent that is found is registered or stopped within a set time.
Scans run continuously, and unregistered agent traffic is blocked.
objectives.evidence: The scan results, the agents found and what happened to each.

objectives.title: Sandboxes for experiments
objectives.statement: Run experimental agents in isolated sandboxes, so that risky trials never touch production systems or data.
objectives.metric: Share of experimental agents in a sandbox
tiers: The experiment runs only in a sandbox with synthetic or public data.
A production agent's new version is tried in a sandbox before release.
Sandboxes for Tier 3 agents copy the production limits, so that a trial behaves as production would.
Sandbox results are kept as part of the release evidence.
objectives.evidence: The sandbox's network and data settings, and the list of agents running in it.
